claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Lower-temperature-manufactured ZrB2 has limited oxidation resistance.
Lower-temperature-manufactured ZrB2 has limited liquid-metal corrosion resistance.
Adding roughly 5 wt% Si to ZrB2 and sintering near 1700 °C will form a Si-rich phase at ZrB2 grain boundaries.
The resulting Si-rich grain-boundary phase will be fine and interconnected.
Silicon lowers the activation energy for sintering ZrB2.
The silicon addition promotes densification of ZrB2 at approximately 1700 °C.
During oxidation service, the Si-rich phase forms a silica or silicate layer.
The silica or silicate layer inhibits oxygen ingress.
The Si-derived layer acts as a physical barrier against corrosion by liquid plating metals.
Si-doped ZrB2 sintered near 1700 °C will attain structural integrity comparable to conventional ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C.
Si-doped ZrB2 sintered near 1700 °C will attain strength comparable to conventional ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C.
Si-doped ZrB2 will have significantly better oxidation resistance than conventional high-temperature-sintered ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
Si-doped ZrB2 will undergo less liquid-metal corrosion than conventional high-temperature-sintered ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
Keeping the silicon addition near 5 wt% avoids detrimental second-phase clusters.
The intervention is applicable near a sintering temperature of 1700 °C in an inert or slightly reducing atmosphere.
The intervention is applicable at service temperatures where the protective silica layer does not volatilize significantly.
Oxidation performance is predicted to improve during exposure in air at approximately 1200–1400 °C.

contradictions.description: The design specifies only Si-doped and undoped specimens both sintered near 1700 °C, whereas the falsification rule and predicted outcome require comparison with high-temperature-sintered ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens. Those required comparator groups are absent from the stated design.
